summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a complex medical history including acute myeloid leukemia in remission after stem cell transplant, anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy with severely reduced ejection fraction (10–13%), end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, and cryptogenic organizing pneumonia on supplemental oxygen, was admitted for recurrent syncope. The episodes, occurring daily and recently at rest, were evaluated with telemetry, echocardiogram, EEG, and CT angiography. No arrhythmias, seizures, or pulmonary embolism were found. The syncope was determined to be multifactorial, primarily due to orthostatic hypotension from end-stage heart failure, with possible vagal and psychogenic components. His adrenal insufficiency was confirmed with a suboptimal cortisol response, leading to an increase in prednisone from 2 mg to 5 mg daily. He remained stable without further syncopal events, continued his vancomycin taper for C. diff, and was cleared for swallowing. Goals of care were discussed, and code status was updated to DNR with intubation allowed. He was discharged home with services, on a stable medication regimen, with follow-up in cardiology, endocrinology, and primary care.
